name: Search for and select an external manager
summary: When the annual investment plan calls for a new or replacement public market mandate (credit, public equities or hedge fund strategies), the manager research team and the sponsoring portfolio manager screen the market, send an RFP and due diligence questionnaire, narrow the field to two or three finalists and run investment and operational due diligence, references, compliance checks and fee negotiation. The portfolio manager writes the memo, the risk team adds an independent opinion and the investment committee decides; the approved terms then go to legal. Most of the four-month elapsed time is waiting for managers' responses, meeting slots and committee dates, and finalists that fail operational due diligence send the team back a stage.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion and 240 staff that cut its external roster from 200 to 124 managers in 2020 and keeps hiring strategic external partners.
baseline.notes: Snapshot of practice in 2021; in 2020 and 2021 most onsite visits were video calls.

trigger: An approved asset class plan, or an opportunistic approach by a manager reopening capacity, calls for a new or replacement external mandate.
end_state: The investment committee has approved the selected manager and the term sheet has been sent to legal, or the search is rejected or cancelled.

volume.seasonality: More searches start in the first half of the year after the annual plan is approved; restructuring years such as 2020 had more.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file's process map; 124 managers after a cut from 200 in 2020 (mgr2020) implies regular replacement searches.

evidence.note: FTE: hands-on time of about 90 hours per search for this role (screening, RFP, ODD, references) at 1.5 searches a month. steps.name: Define mandate need and search criteria
steps.description: The sponsoring portfolio manager turns the approved asset class plan into a search request: why a new or replacement mandate is needed, target size, benchmark, style, tracking error range, fee budget, vehicle (separate account or pooled fund) and a timetable. They check the current roster in the research database for overlap and draft the screening criteria.

error.defect_description: Criteria too narrow or too loose, so the long list is poor.

control.basis: Investment plan and delegated authority: a search starts only for a mandate in the approved asset class plan

evidence.note: nc_imd: the asset class director proposes the rationale, staff and consultant roles and search criteria. The model manager rebuilt its roster in 2020 (mgr2020). Times and waits are tier C estimates.

steps.name: Approve search scope
steps.description: The asset class managing director reviews the search request with the head of manager research, confirms the mandate size against the plan and agrees who runs the search, then approves it by email with the CIO copied. Requests with unclear rationale go back to the portfolio manager.

control.basis: Delegated authority: managing director approves search rationale and criteria with CIO concurrence (practice described in nc_imd)

next.condition: sent back for a clearer rationale or criteria

evidence.note: nc_imd: rationale, roles and criteria are approved by the CIO before screening. Return rate tier C.

steps.name: Screen manager universe and build long list
steps.description: The manager research analyst screens vendor and consultant manager databases, peer information and internal research notes for firms meeting the criteria on assets, track record length, style and capacity, then ranks them on risk-adjusted returns. They agree a long list of about 8 to 15 firms to receive the RFP.

error.defect_description: A suitable firm is missed because its database entry is stale.

evidence.note: Both describe screening consultant databases and internal files to eliminate firms early; nc_imd sends requests to typically 3 or more managers. Long list size and times tier C.

steps.name: Issue RFP and due diligence questionnaire
steps.description: The analyst adapts the standard RFP and due diligence questionnaire (AIMA or in-house format) to the mandate, adds the fee proposal template and confidentiality terms and sends them to the long list with a response deadline. Questions from managers are answered to all candidates.

control.basis: Manager research procedure: same RFP, DDQ and deadline for every candidate so responses can be compared

evidence.note: AIMA DDQ modules and standard comparison; GFOA RFP criteria; bpm_search on an RFP with a schedule and fee breakdown. Times tier C.

steps.name: Managers prepare RFP responses
steps.description: Candidate managers complete the RFP, questionnaire and fee proposal and send performance data, holdings and team biographies. Some decline because capacity is closed. The research team waits for the deadline.

evidence.note: gsic_ocio gives 4 to 6 weeks for RFP issuance and response; 10 to 21 days for the response window is the author's estimate within that.

steps.name: Log responses and check completeness
steps.description: The analyst files each response in the research database, checks that every required section, document and the fee proposal are present, and loads return series into the analysis workbook. Gaps are listed for a chase.

evidence.note: Common practice; share of incomplete responses is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase missing information
steps.description: The analyst emails the managers with incomplete responses, lists the missing items and checks what comes back against the list before the evaluation starts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of manager reply times.

steps.name: Evaluate and score responses
steps.description: The analyst, with input from the portfolio manager, scores each response on organisation, team, process, track record over three, five and ten years, risk, operations and fees using a weighted scorecard, and runs returns and holdings analysis in the risk system to check style and factor exposures against the claimed approach.

error.defect_description: Return series not net of fees or benchmark mismatched, flattering a candidate.

evidence.note: GFOA lists organisational, investment, fee and operational criteria and 3, 5 and 10 year performance; bpm_search recommends a scorecard. Times tier C.

steps.name: Agree shortlist
steps.description: The head of manager research meets the portfolio manager and analyst, challenges the scores and agrees three or four semi-finalists. If no candidate fits, the criteria are reopened with the portfolio manager.

evidence.note: Initial evaluation narrows to three to five finalists (gsic_ocio). Re-scope rate tier C.

steps.name: Hold preliminary calls with semi-finalists
steps.description: The portfolio manager holds an hour-long call with each semi-finalist on strategy, capacity, operations, conflicts and willingness to accept the organisation's standard terms and fee levels, and makes informal reference calls to peers. One or two firms are usually dropped.

evidence.note: nc_imd describes preliminary conference calls on operations, risk, compliance, conflicts and preferred terms, with informal reference calls. Times tier C.

steps.name: Conduct investment due diligence on finalists
steps.description: The portfolio manager runs deep-dive sessions with each finalist's portfolio managers and analysts, reviews sample research, trade and risk processes, rebuilds attribution from holdings and tests how past underperformance was handled. Notes and a draft assessment go into the research database.

error.defect_description: Key person dependence or capacity limits underweighted.

evidence.note: Investment due diligence on process, people and performance is described by both. Times tier C.

steps.name: Visit finalists' offices
steps.description: The portfolio manager and analyst visit each finalist's office, often in New York, London or Boston, to meet the wider team, watch the investment meeting and see trading and risk systems. In 2020 and 2021 most visits were video calls.

evidence.note: sbai2024: 60% of institutional investors conduct onsite reviews for new managers, 7% do not; virtual reviews were used during COVID-19. Times tier C.

steps.name: Call references
steps.description: The analyst calls three to five current and former clients of each finalist, preferably in the same strategy, using a standard question list on service, reporting, errors and how the manager handled poor periods.

evidence.note: Both require references from other institutional clients. Counts and times tier C.

steps.name: Review operational due diligence documents
steps.description: The analyst, acting as operational due diligence reviewer, reads the operations, compliance and risk sections of the questionnaire and the supporting documents: controls report (SOC 1), audited financial statements, compliance manual, valuation and trade error policies, regulatory registration and insurance. They confirm custodian, administrator and auditor relationships directly with those firms.

error.defect_description: A control weakness in trade allocation or valuation is missed.

evidence.note: aima_journal: documents collected and reviewed before meetings; GFOA lists SOC reports and back office. sbai2024: 77% do a full ODD review for a new manager. Times tier C.

steps.name: Hold operational due diligence meeting
steps.description: The analyst meets the finalist's chief operating officer, chief compliance officer and head of operations, walks through trade flow, reconciliations, cash controls and cyber security, and focuses on the issues found in the documents.

evidence.note: aima_journal: ODD meetings now run at least twice as long as the couple of hours they once took, focused on the highest-risk areas. Waits tier C.

steps.name: Sign off operational due diligence rating
steps.description: The head of manager research reviews the operational due diligence report and approves a pass, a pass with conditions to be written into the agreement, or a fail. A failed finalist is replaced by the runner-up, and the search is cancelled if no finalist passes.

control.basis: Operational due diligence policy: a pass rating is required before a manager is recommended; ODD has an effective veto

next.condition: fail, next finalist taken into due diligence

evidence.note: sbai2024: 32% of dedicated ODD teams have a formal veto and 15% an effective one, used rarely. Fail and cancel rates are tier C.

steps.name: Run compliance and conflict checks
steps.description: The compliance analyst checks the selected firm's securities registrations and disciplinary history, screens the firm and principals against sanctions and adverse media, collects conflict of interest declarations from staff on the search and confirms any placement agent disclosures.

control.basis: Code of business conduct, conflict of interest and placement agent disclosure rules (independent compliance review as in nc_imd)

evidence.note: nc_imd requires an independent compliance review and conflict certifications; GFOA requires conflict disclosure. Rates and times tier C.

steps.name: Choose preferred manager
steps.description: The managing director reviews the investment and operational findings, references and fee proposals with the portfolio manager and head of manager research and chooses the preferred manager and a runner-up.

evidence.note: Final evaluation and selection phase of 2 to 3 weeks (gsic_ocio). Times tier C.

steps.name: Negotiate fees and key terms
steps.description: The portfolio manager negotiates the fee schedule, breakpoints, most favoured nation fee protection, capacity commitment and the vehicle with the preferred manager, comparing the offer with fees paid for similar mandates.

evidence.note: gsic_ocio places fee negotiation in final selection; the model manager reported $10 million of fee savings in 2020 (mgr2020). Times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for manager's revised fee offer
steps.description: The manager takes the request to its pricing committee and replies with a revised fee schedule and term positions. A second round is common.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of manager pricing committee turnaround and round count.

steps.name: Draft investment memo
steps.description: The portfolio manager, with the analyst, writes the investment committee memo: mandate rationale, comparison of finalists, investment and operational findings, references, agreed fees, expected value added, risks, funding source and the client portfolios or pool that will hold the mandate.

error.defect_description: Gaps in the risk discussion or unsupported value-added estimate.

evidence.note: nc_imd lists the contents of an investment recommendation memo. Times tier C.

steps.name: Review memo
steps.description: The managing director reads the memo, checks sizing against the asset class plan and sends comments. Most memos go through one round of edits.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of review time and edit rate.

steps.name: Obtain independent risk opinion
steps.description: The investment risk manager reviews the memo for fit with the risk budget, expected tracking error, concentration, liquidity and key person risk and writes the risk opinion attached to the committee paper. Questions sometimes require memo changes.

control.basis: Investment risk policy: independent risk opinion required for every new mandate paper (see new-investment-risk-review)

next.condition: memo revised to answer risk questions

evidence.note: The organisation file's new-investment-risk-review process describes this; times and revision rate tier C.

steps.name: Submit paper to investment committee
steps.description: The investment office checks the paper against the committee template, adds it to the next agenda and circulates the pack. Papers wait for the next scheduled committee and its submission deadline.

evidence.note: Committee cadence assumed every two to three weeks; detail in investment-committee-approval.

steps.name: Investment committee decides
steps.description: The investment committee, chaired by the CIO with the CEO and chief risk officer, hears the portfolio manager, questions the case and approves, approves with conditions, defers for more work or rejects. The decision is minuted by the investment office.

control.basis: Investment committee terms of reference and delegated authority limits approved by the board

evidence.note: Committee approval after memo and compliance review (nc_imd); sbai2024: ODD results reported to the investment committee. Outcome shares tier C.

steps.name: Notify finalists and record decision
steps.description: The analyst tells unsuccessful finalists the outcome, keeps the runner-up warm until contracts are signed, and records the decision, scorecards and due diligence files in the research database.

evidence.note: Notifying participants is part of final selection (gsic_ocio); nc_imd asks for prompt communication with eliminated managers. Times tier C.

steps.name: Send legal instruction
steps.description: The portfolio manager sends investment counsel the term sheet: agreed fees, draft investment guidelines, vehicle, owning accounts and any operational conditions from the due diligence, starting negotiation of the management agreement.

error.defect_description: Guideline wording differs from what was approved, a source of later breaches.

evidence.note: Negotiation and contracting follow approval (nc_imd). Times tier C.

exceptions.name: Finalist fails operational due diligence
exceptions.description: The ODD review finds a material control weakness (valuation, cash controls, trade allocation) that the manager will not fix; the runner-up is taken through investment due diligence.

exceptions.name: No suitable candidates on the shortlist
exceptions.description: Scores show no firm meets the criteria at an acceptable fee, so the portfolio manager revises the criteria and the screen is rerun.

exceptions.name: Committee defers the paper
exceptions.description: The committee asks for more analysis (for example on sizing or fees) and the memo returns to the next meeting.

exceptions.name: Search cancelled
exceptions.description: No finalist passes operational due diligence; the mandate is covered internally or the search restarts later.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from search request to committee approval and legal instruction
benchmarks.population: Public market manager searches at Canadian and US public asset owners (author's synthesis)

evidence.note: gsic_ocio gives 4 to 6 months from RFP preparation to contract signing for an outsourced manager search; this workflow stops before contract signing, so the median is set at about 4 months. The organisation file says three to six months.
RFP issuance and response 4 to 6 weeks plus initial evaluation 2 to 3 weeks.

pain_points.description: Investment and operational due diligence on several finalists piles up on a small research team; 41% of ODD professionals say they do not always have enough time for a review.
Bespoke RFPs and questionnaires are re-keyed into scoring workbooks, so comparing managers is slow and error-prone.

evidence.note: 59% of investors use bespoke DDQs (sbai2024); AIMA's standard DDQ exists to allow like-for-like comparison.

pain_points.description: Papers wait for the next committee date and memo rework loops add weeks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on committee cadence.

pain_points.description: Fee negotiation runs through the manager's pricing committee in rounds.

evidence.note: Common practice.

sources.title: External Investment Manager and Vehicle Selection Policy and Procedures (IMD-POL-1001)
sources.publisher: North Carolina Department of State Treasurer, Investment Management Division
sources.supports: Public pension manager and fund selection steps: director proposes search rationale, staff and consultant roles and criteria for CIO approval; first-level database screen and short-form questionnaire; requests for information to typically 3 or more managers; screen of responses; preliminary conference calls covering operations, risk, compliance, conflicts and willingness to accept preferred terms, with informal reference calls; finalist interviews with CIO, risk, operations and compliance invited. For private funds: annual work plan sets commitment pace; opportunity database; preliminary fund screen; intensive due diligence (PPM review, performance and fee analysis, comparison with competing offerings, presentations or onsite visits, reference checks, risk and operational review, conflicts, placement agent forms, willingness to accept preferred terms); limited partnership offering periods cycle every 4 to 6 years; investment recommendation memo with SWOT; documents requested (code of ethics, compliance manual, valuation policy, SSAE 16 report, insurance, ADV, audited financials); independent compliance review; conditional approval before negotiation; external counsel negotiates and writes a memo comparing terms with preferred terms; final approval and execution; no-contact communication protocol.

sources.title: Selecting Third-Party Investment Professionals for Pension Fund Assets (best practice)
sources.supports: Competitive, merit-based selection run by a consultant or review committee; candidate sources (consultant databases, references from other plans); conflict disclosure; RFP evaluation criteria (organisational, financial, investment, fee, operational); review of track record over 3, 5 and 10 years, risk management, back office and SOC 2 type reports; references from other pension clients and a presentation by the decision makers; management agreement terms; at least annual due diligence review of policy compliance and performance.

sources.title: Due Diligence Questionnaires (2019)
sources.supports: AIMA Illustrative Questionnaire for the Due Diligence of Investment Managers with modules for overview, governance, operations and risk management and fund terms, plus strategy modules (hedge fund, private credit, private equity) and topic modules (responsible investment, cyber security, outsourcing). Investors use it as an early step that guides further questions; standard questions let investors compare responses from several managers like for like.

sources.title: Operational due diligence: what are investors seeking? (AIMA Journal, edition 120)
sources.supports: ODD teams collect documents before meetings, focus meeting time on the highest-risk areas and review policies, compliance controls and legal documents; ODD meetings now run at least twice as long as the couple of hours they once took; private market managers sometimes ask for a review on a week's notice, which panellists called impractical.

sources.title: SBAI 2024 Operational Due Diligence Practices Survey
sources.supports: 70% of responding institutional investors have dedicated ODD teams, 80% of which report outside the investment function; 77% do a full ODD review at the start of a new manager relationship; 60% conduct onsite reviews for new managers and 7% do not; results go to the investment committee alone for 50%; 32% of ODD teams have a formal veto, used rarely or at most once a year by 73% of those; only 7% monitor managers less than annually, with a trend to risk-based monitoring; 59% use bespoke DDQs; 41% say they do not always have enough time to complete an ODD review; for private markets ODD is often embedded in the investment team's due diligence.

sources.title: OCIO search guidance (foundation impact investing toolkit)
sources.supports: Phases of an outsourced investment manager search: preparation 4 to 6 weeks, RFP issuance and response 4 to 6 weeks, initial evaluation 2 to 3 weeks to three to five finalists, finalist presentations 2 to 4 weeks, final evaluation and selection 2 to 3 weeks (reference checks, fee negotiation, notifying participants); 4 to 6 months from RFP preparation to contract signing.

sources.title: Lessons learned during an investment manager search
sources.supports: A Canadian foundation's manager search: define priorities first, issue a detailed RFP with a schedule, compare offerings and fee components, deliberate in committee; the author would add an itemised fee breakdown and a scorecard and describes the effort as enormous.

sources.title: The model manager posts solid 2020 return, meets benchmark index (news release)
sources.publisher: The model manager via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: External manager roster cut from 200 to 124 in 2020, fund-of-funds eliminated, new strategic partnerships; $10 million of investment management fees saved; 2020 private commitments: three mid-market buyout fund commitments totalling $1 billion, real estate funds (KingSett Affordable Housing, Breakthrough Life Science, Dermody Industrial III), credit funds (Sagard Credit Partners II, Oaktree Opportunities XI).

sources.title: Wages: Financial Analyst near Toronto (ON), NOC 11101
sources.supports: Toronto region hourly wages low $27.97, median $41.60, high $73.57 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: Steps show a credit search (md_global_credit, pm_global_credit). Public equity and public market alternatives searches follow the same steps with md_public_equities, pm_public_equities, md_pma and pm_pma; FTE is split across them by an assumed share of searches (credit 40%, equities 35%, alternatives 25%).

pm_public_equities is not listed among the process map roles but does the portfolio manager steps in equity searches; compliance_analyst, investment_risk_manager, investment_office_manager and cio appear for short steps that link to other processes.

The independent risk review and the committee decision are documented in detail in new-investment-risk-review and investment-committee-approval; they appear here as single steps so that their elapsed time counts in the search.
The manager research analysts also act as operational due diligence reviewers, as the organisation file's role title says; there is no separate ODD team.
Triggers: 80% of searches start from the annual plan and 20% from an opportunistic approach by a manager (manager_rfp_response), reflecting the opportunistic search path in nc_imd.
Branch probabilities (rework, ODD fail 9%, deferral 9%, rejection 3%, cancellation 3%) are the author's estimates.

Hands-on time of roughly 200 to 230 hours per search (about 100 for the sponsoring portfolio manager and 90 for the research analyst) is the author's estimate; with 1.5 searches a month this needs about 2.5 FTE across the roles.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (Job Bank wages deflated to 2021, variable pay and a 1.35 loading for staff, total-pay estimates for investment professionals).
